extracted.intended_audience: early-career neuroscientists applying for the McKnight Scholar Award (and their institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for the McKnight Scholar Awards, a foundation grant supporting exceptional early-career neuroscientists establishing independent laboratories. Includes eligibility, expectations about research impact, mentoring and inclusive lab commitments, allowable budget items, IP and dissemination requirements, and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage-of-career / independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scholar Awards are given to exceptional young scientists who are in the early stages of establishing an independent laboratory and research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be at the early stage of establishing an independent lab and research career; the program is intended to support those beginning independent research trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence / exceptional candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are given to 'exceptional young scientists' — applicants must demonstrate outstanding promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates who have shown exceptional ability and promise in neuroscience research; the program’s history highlights major discoveries by past Scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research impact / ability to solve significant problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate their ability to solve significant problems in neuroscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program’s intent is to foster commitment to research careers that will have an important impact on the study of the brain. Projects that address major problems in the field — including work that may translate basic research to clinical practice — are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to mentoring neuroscientists from underrepresented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks to support scientists committed to mentoring neuroscientists from underrepresented groups at all levels of training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should document a demonstrated or planned commitment to mentoring individuals from underrepresented backgrounds across training levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to an equitable and inclusive lab environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to an equitable and inclusive lab environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence or plans for fostering equity and inclusion within the lab (policies, practices, mentorship, recruitment) are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field / disciplinary focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be neuroscientists; the program supports neuroscience research specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed research should fall within neuroscience; the Foundation highlights neuroscience discoveries made by past Scholars as illustrative of the program’s focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award term and amount (selection logistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to ten McKnight Scholars will be selected to receive three years of support, beginning June 1, 2026. The total award is $225,000 paid in equal installments of $75,000 in 2026, 2027, and 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection will be limited (up to ten awards); applicants should plan budgets consistent with a three‑year project and the specified payment schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable budget items
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable budget items include salaries and fringe benefits, tuition, equipment, supplies, animal costs, costs for technical services, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should budget for direct costs of running a lab and project-specific expenses within these categories. Use the award to support the investigator’s research activities as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds cannot be used for indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests must not include institutional overhead/indirect cost recovery; plan direct costs only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and dissemination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property rights resulting from the research (including patents, copyrights, processes, or formulae) will be retained by the institution of the awardee. The information derived from the research will be published in a form that is available to the interested public and made available to the public on a nondiscriminatory basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees/institutions retain IP ownership, but results must be published and otherwise disseminated openly and non-discriminatorily to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in the McKnight community / conference expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Award winners attend the McKnight Conference on Neuroscience for the three years after receiving the award, and then return to the conference every three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholars should be prepared to engage with the McKnight community: attend the annual conference for three consecutive years, present (especially third‑year awardees), and participate in ongoing community interactions and collaborations.
